Uses and Administration Rosiglitazone is a thiazolidinedione oral antidiabetic that improves insulin sensitivity and is used for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus (p.431). It is usu- ally given as rosiglitazone maleate but doses are ex- pressed in terms of the base; rosiglitazone maleate 1.32 mg is equivalent to about 1 mg of rosiglitazone. The potassium salt is used in some countries. Rosigli- tazone is given orally as monotherapy, particularly in patients who are overweight and for whom metformin is contra-indicated or not tolerated. It may also be add- ed to metformin, a sulfonylurea (or a combination of the two), or to insulin, when such therapy is inadequate (but see Administration, below). The usual initial dose is 4 mg daily, given in a single dose or two divided dos- es. The dose may be increased to a maximum of 8 mg daily if necessary after 8 to 12 weeks in patients receiv- ing monotherapy or combination oral therapy. Rosigli- tazone may be taken with or without food. ◊ References. 1. Nolan JJ, et al. Rosiglitazone taken once daily provides effec- tive glycaemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
